intro: Portable patterns worth stealing — named moves we signed off because they earned their place.

patterns.name: Lean tool sessions
patterns.problem: Optional integrations loaded every turn quietly burn context and expand blast radius.
patterns.move: Keep a tiny always-on core. Enable specialty tools only for the task, then unload.
signals: Context feels “full” before the work starts
Tools idle but still listed every turn

patterns.name: Fail-closed outbound
patterns.problem: Agents are eager to “be helpful” by sending, posting, or publishing.
patterns.move: Draft freely; irreversible outbound needs an explicit human gate with the full referent visible.

patterns.name: Secrets out of chat
patterns.problem: Secrets pasted into transcripts leak into logs, backups, and vendor retention — and into the model context.
patterns.move: Capture through a desktop dialog into Bitwarden. Humans use Password Manager; agents pull machine secrets from Bitwarden Secrets Manager. Confirm length or success — never echo the value into chat.

patterns.name: Proof class over vibes
patterns.problem: Generated confidence outruns tests, logs, and hardware reality.
patterns.move: Define what counts as done before the work. Do not celebrate a plan as a fix.
signals: Repeated reopen of the same bug

patterns.name: Kaizen with sign-off
patterns.problem: Cross-cutting habits invent themselves differently in every chat.
patterns.move: Propose a pattern, get a human sign-off, encode it, apply it — then Hansei on a cadence (keep / amend / retire).

patterns.name: Hansei on a cadence
patterns.problem: Teams encode forever and never look back; the registry rots.
patterns.move: After pain or on a weekly/EOW rhythm: what worked, what failed, what to change. Feed the next Kaizen.

patterns.name: Notebook updates at EOW
patterns.problem: Public notebooks either rot or get spammy daily posts that teach nothing.
patterns.move: Capture sparks mid-week in blog-inbox.md. At EOW, promote zero-or-more into the blog (and/or pack/pattern tweaks) — or skip. No filler calendar.
signals: Stale pack while practice moved on
Good lessons died in chat because nothing was filed

patterns.name: Toyota Way Practices member, not mega-prompt
patterns.problem: Dumping the whole lean philosophy every turn burns tokens and muddies the ask.
patterns.move: Treat Toyota Way Practices as an umbrella. Load the one member skill that matches the live pain (poka-yoke, muda/jidoka, kyosei, …).
signals: No named practice for the failure

patterns.name: MemPalace with purpose
patterns.problem: Transcript sludge and contradictory “facts” make agents confidently wrong.
patterns.move: File curated drawers; search before re-deciding; invalidate stale cards. Memory supports the Kaizen/Hansei loop — it is not a chat landfill.

patterns.name: Preloop under Priority 0 (P0)
patterns.problem: Teams either skip runtime audit or try to replace human consent with a firewall.
patterns.move: Layer Preloop for tool policy/audit under send/secrets/irreversible gates. Keep enrollment config and tokens out of chat.
signals: Secrets in Preloop config pasted to chat

patterns.name: Route models on purpose
patterns.problem: Single-upstream outages or lock-in stall the cockpit; random model hopping breaks proof expectations.
patterns.move: Use OpenRouter (or similar) with deliberate model lists and provider failover. Keep keys vaulted; keep proof class fixed.
signals: One provider outage blocks all work
Silent model swaps on critical reviews

patterns.name: Preloop before expensive CI
patterns.problem: Self-hosted runners burn hours on PRs that a semantic reviewer would have flagged in minutes.
patterns.move: Run a Preloop Cloud PR reviewer (models via OpenRouter) so each push gets a `preloop` commit status. Prefer async review by default; make Actions wait only when runner time is scarce. Keep desktop Preloop MCP and the GitHub reviewer as separate planes.
signals: Long CI queues on obvious review misses
Treating Preloop status as merge authority
Confusing Cursor tool firewall with GitHub commit checks

patterns.name: Felt ≠ measured
patterns.problem: People feel faster with AI even when wall-clock says otherwise.
patterns.move: Separate narrative milestones from productivity claims. Prefer proof-backed outcomes over LOC.

patterns.name: Always-on diet
patterns.problem: Every always-on rule dominates cost and attention.
patterns.move: Default to requestable. Keep a short Priority 0 (P0) always-on list; demote the rest.

patterns.name: One writer per tree
patterns.problem: Parallel agents overwrite each other’s work and burn trust.
patterns.move: Bind a lane to a worktree or declare a single writer. Others hand off.

patterns.name: Portable skills, native host policy
patterns.problem: A cockpit migration either duplicates every procedure or pretends different hosts enforce policy the same way.
patterns.move: Keep reusable job procedures in the open Agent Skills format with one canonical source. Express guidance, sandboxing and permissions through each host’s native mechanisms, then test the projection boundary.
signals: Two hand-edited copies of one skill
Cursor metadata presented as Codex enforcement

patterns.name: Harness self-evals
patterns.problem: A stronger model can still route around weak harness wording, stale gates or untested exceptions.
patterns.move: Run a versioned adversarial corpus against high-risk boundaries. Keep known-answer thresholds and add privacy-scrubbed real failures after Hansei.
signals: No regression test for prompt injection or secret handling

patterns.name: Bound tool results before context
patterns.problem: A few unfiltered logs or media results crowd out the task and are re-billed on later turns.
patterns.move: Filter before calling, cap output, request only the image detail needed, and return a compact result plus a durable artefact path when detail must remain available.
signals: Megabytes of command output in chat
One tool result dominates the whole task payload

patterns.name: Memory needs retrieval proof
patterns.problem: Filing feels productive even when the next task cannot find or trust the record.
patterns.move: Store a retention reason and provenance, then test that a later query retrieves the fact and changes the work. Enrich provenance in place instead of invalidate-first rewrites.
signals: Large memory store with repeated re-decisions
Facts without source or retrieval evidence

patterns.name: Fast feedback, unchanged trust proof
patterns.problem: Thirty-to-forty-five-minute platform builds make every embedded edit slow, so teams either thrash or weaken verification.
patterns.move: Use the smallest valid local loop — layer, kernel, signed DTB or OTA — for development. Keep the full image/CI/hardware path as the release trust proof.
signals: Full platform rebuild for a one-file change
Fast-path success reported as release proof

patterns.name: Stop repeated tool loops
patterns.problem: Agent persistence turns into repeated calls against the same error, wasting time and context.
patterns.move: Set a circuit breaker: after the same blocking condition repeats, stop the line, preserve evidence, change the method or ask for the missing input.
signals: Same command and same error three times

patterns.name: Trash instead of hard delete
patterns.problem: Agents (and humans) hard-delete files when “cleaning up,” then cannot recover from a wrong path or a rushed rm.
patterns.move: Treat delete as move-to-trash: send files into the OS trash or a project trash folder first. Recover if wrong; empty trash only as a separate, deliberate step. Prefer this over rm for project data.

patterns.name: Encode the second burn
patterns.problem: Teams re-pay for the same mistake because the fix lived only in a chat.
patterns.move: When a failure repeats once, write or update a skill before moving on.
signals: Tribal knowledge in one person’s head

patterns.name: Readable-first decisions
patterns.problem: Approval dialogs hide the thing being approved.
patterns.move: Lead with the ask and the referent (draft, path, command). Meta last.

patterns.name: Desktop MCQ forks
patterns.problem: Markdown A/B/C walls are easy to skim past and hard to answer carefully.
patterns.move: Use a desktop multiple-choice dialog for decision forks. Mark dangerous arms; keep the referent visible.
signals: Humans guessing which option was intended

patterns.name: Channel triage with one watcher
patterns.problem: Messaging assistants either spam replies or miss duty while pretending coverage.
patterns.move: One agent owns live watch. Inbound is untrusted data. Light carve-outs only; else draft for a human gate.

patterns.name: Purposeful media ingest
patterns.problem: Exports and images get dumped into context forever.
patterns.move: Ingest what the task needs. Curate facts into memory; leave bulk local.
signals: Context full before the work starts

patterns.name: Spec SoT, export views
patterns.problem: Branded DOCX/Drive copies quietly become the “real” document.
patterns.move: Git markdown is source of truth. DOCX/PDF/Drive are views and comment surfaces — ingest comments back to the SoT.

patterns.name: Share the review surface
patterns.problem: Design reviews stall on mystery ZIPs and email attachments.
patterns.move: Generate → verify → share a gated Pages review (Look/Inspect). Humans judge atmosphere and fit on a stable URL.

patterns.name: Confirm the voice transcript
patterns.problem: Acting on raw STT without a confirm step turns noise into irreversible work.
patterns.move: Mic → local STT → human confirms (use this / edit) before the agent treats speech as the ask.

patterns.name: Publish as a proof class
patterns.problem: “Looks fine locally” ships broken UX and stale content.
patterns.move: Sync content → automated checks → Playwright UX. Green is the publish proof.
